name: Primary Myelofibrosis

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: WHO 2022 Diagnostic Criteria for Primary Myelofibrosis

criteria.description: Megakaryocyte proliferation and atypia, accompanied by reticulin and/or collagen fibrosis grade >= 2 (overt PMF) or grade 0-1 (pre-fibrotic PMF)
Not meeting WHO criteria for ET, PV, BCR-ABL1+ CML, MDS, or other myeloid neoplasm
Presence of JAK2, CALR, or MPL mutation, or other clonal marker
Anemia not attributable to comorbid condition

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: All 3 major criteria plus at least 1 minor criterion (for overt PMF); all 3 major criteria plus at least 1 minor criterion (for pre-fibrotic PMF)
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Pre-fibrotic PMF has a better prognosis than overt PMF. DIPSS and MIPSS70 scores used for risk stratification.

pathognomonic.notes: Spleen may extend to pelvis; due to extramedullary hematopoiesis

pathognomonic.symptomName: Leukoerythroblastic blood smear with teardrop cells (dacrocytes)
pathognomonic.notes: Teardrop-shaped red cells plus nucleated RBCs and immature myeloid cells

rare.symptomName: Extramedullary hematopoiesis causing spinal cord compression

rare.notes: Blast transformation occurs in 10-20% over disease course

laboratory: Leukoerythroblastic blood smear with teardrop cells (dacrocytes)
Variable white cell count (may be elevated or decreased)
Variable platelet count (may be elevated or decreased)
JAK2 V617F (~60%), CALR (~25%), or MPL (~7%) mutation
imaging: Abdominal imaging showing massive splenomegaly and often hepatomegaly
Bone scan or MRI may show osteosclerosis
genetic: Additional high-molecular-risk mutations: ASXL1, EZH2, SRSF2, IDH1/2, U2AF1
other: Bone marrow biopsy showing reticulin and/or collagen fibrosis (grade 2-3)
Atypical megakaryocytes with cloud-like or balloon-like nuclei
Dry tap on bone marrow aspiration common

distinguishingFeatures: Post-PV myelofibrosis develops after documented PV
Minimal or no fibrosis on marrow biopsy
Post-ET myelofibrosis develops after documented ET
Marked leukocytosis with left shift and basophilia
MDS shows dysplasia in hematopoietic lineages
No driver mutations (JAK2, CALR, MPL) typically

redFlags: Transformation to acute myeloid leukemia (blast crisis)
Massive splenomegaly causing splenic infarction or rupture
specialistType: Transplant Hematologist (for allogeneic stem cell transplant evaluation)
references: Arber DA, et al. The 2016 revision to the World Health Organization classification of myeloid neoplasms and acute leukemia. Blood. 2016;127(20):2391-2405.

Guglielmelli P, et al. MIPSS70: Mutation-Enhanced International Prognostic Score System for transplantation-age patients with primary myelofibrosis. J Clin Oncol. 2018;36(4):310-318.
